explain: stage2 now reads the lo, hi and v1 that stage1 wrote in the same cycle, so the product appears one cycle after the input (3 × 4 = 12 at cycle 1). Those registers are still written, but nothing reads their stored values any more, so synthesis removes them (17 flip-flops instead of 42). The multiply and the add become one combinational path into p, and the depth grows from 22 to 33.

One rule computes the full 8×8 product in one cycle. It has one cycle of latency, 17 flip-flops instead of 42, and a combinational path of depth 30 instead of the two-stage version's 22. The pipeline register is what splits that path in two.
